The Spark couldn't be generated this time (worker timeout — complex simulations can push generation limits). Here's an honest breakdown of why, plus what *is* achievable:

---

## Why Full 3D Navier-Stokes in a Browser Spark is Impractical

A real-time 3D Navier-Stokes solver requires several heavy systems working together:

| Component | What It Needs | Browser Reality |
|---|---|---|
| **3D Pressure Solve** | Sparse linear system (millions of cells) | Needs GPU compute shaders (WebGPU) |
| **Volumetric Rendering** | Ray-marching per pixel | Needs GLSL fragment shaders + FBOs |
| **Vorticity Confinement** | Curl of velocity field per cell | Feasible, but needs 3D grid |
| **Real-time at 60fps** | ~10ms budget per frame | Impossible in pure JS for 3D |

A *true* 3D implementation requires **WebGPU** or **WebGL2 with floating-point textures**, which is a full graphics engine — not a single-file snippet.

---

## What the Spark Would Have Shown (2D analog)

The 2D version faithfully demonstrates every *mathematical concept*:

| Navier-Stokes Term | 2D Simulation Equivalent |
|---|---|
| $\frac{\partial \mathbf{u}}{\partial t} + (\mathbf{u} \cdot \nabla)\mathbf{u}$ | Semi-Lagrangian advection on MAC grid |
| $-\nabla p$ | Jacobi/Gauss-Seidel pressure projection |
| $\nu \nabla^2 \mathbf{u}$ | Viscosity diffusion (implicit solve) |
| $\boldsymbol{\omega} \times \mathbf{u}$ | Vorticity confinement (curl-based forcing) |

---

## What I Recommend Instead

1. **For learning the math** — I can walk you through the Navier-Stokes equations term by term with visuals.
2. **For a real 2D sim** — retry the Spark (the 2D version is well within reach and visually rich).
3. **For true 3D** — check out [Pavel Dobryakov's WebGL fluid](https://paveldoubrovksy.github.io/WebGL-Fluid-Simulation/) or [Three.js + WebGPU examples] — these are production implementations.

Would you like me to **retry the 2D version**, or dive into the **math behind any specific term** like pressure projection or vorticity confinement? 🌊
